I keep hearing about 'compound interest' but I honestly have no idea how it actually works or why it matters.

Compound interest means you earn interest not just on your original money, but also on the interest that money has already earned. Imagine you invest $1,000 at 5% annual interest. Year 1: you earn $50 (total $1,050). Year 2: you earn 5% on $1,050 = $52.50 (total $1,102.50). Year 3: 5% on $1,102.50 = $55.13. The interest itself grows each year. Over decades, this snowball effect turns modest savings into large sums — that's why starting early matters far more than saving more later.
